examples.en: One moment. Let me check my notes.
Hold on, my wallet's gone.
Just a moment. I have a phone call.
Wait! I'm coming with you.

examples.ko: 여기요, 물 좀 주세요. — 네, 잠깐만요.
examples.en: Excuse me, some water please. — Yes, one moment.
Just a moment, I'll take my wallet out of my bag.

phrases.en: Wait a sec! Where is my bag?
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for friends or younger people.

phrases.en: One moment, I'll take a call.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 더 정중해서 처음 보는 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bit more polite, so it can be used with people you've just met.

phrases.en: Please wait a moment. I'll be right back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기다려 달라고 분명히 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you clearly ask someone to wait.

explain_en: 잠깐만요 is shorter and softer than ‘please wait’. With friends, say 잠깐만.

examples.en: One moment, I'll go get the person in charge.
Excuse me, I'm just going to pass through this narrow path.
One moment, customer. I'll check the order again.
One moment. I'll call you back later.
One moment, I'll go see if there's a seat.
The child said “just a moment” and ran into the room.

explain: '잠깐만요'와 거의 같지만 조금 더 정중해서 손님이나 처음 보는 사람에게 많이 써요. 사람들 사이를 지나갈 때 '잠시만요'라고 하면 '지나갈게요'의 뜻도 돼요. 반말은 '잠시만'이에요.

phrases.en: One moment, let me finish this first.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech used between close people.

phrases.en: Please wait a moment. It will be ready soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손님에게 말할 때 자주 쓰는 정중한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite phrase often used when speaking to customers.

phrases.en: Wait a moment, I'll go with you.
phrases.nuance_en: A little more casual and friendly than the original phrase.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '잠깐만요' but slightly more polite, so people use it a lot with customers or strangers. When you pass through a crowd, '잠시만요' also works as 'excuse me, coming through'. The casual form is '잠시만'.

examples.en: Excuse me. Could I have the menu?
Excuse me, could we get some water?
Excuse me, I don't have a spoon.
Excuse me! More kimchi, please.
Excuse me, where is the restroom?

examples.ko: 여기요, 물 한 잔 더 주세요.
examples.en: Excuse me, one more glass of water, please.

explain: 식당이나 카페에서 직원을 부를 때 가장 흔히 써요. 길에서 모르는 사람을 부를 때는 '저기요'를 많이 쓰고, 출석에서 대답할 때는 '여기요'가 '저 여기 있어요'라는 뜻이에요. 크게 소리치기보다 손을 살짝 들고 부르면 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Excuse me, you dropped your wallet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 모르는 사람을 부를 때 많이 써요. 식당에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to call a stranger on the street. It can also be used in restaurants.

phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 건네거나 내가 여기 있다고 대답할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when handing something over or saying you are here.

phrases.en: Excuse me, could I have some water?
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 식당이나 가게에서 주인을 부를 때 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A friendly way to call the owner in a small restaurant or shop.

dict_examples.en: Excuse me, I'd like to order.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: This is the most common way to call staff at a restaurant or cafe. For calling a stranger on the street, '저기요' is more usual, and when answering a roll call, '여기요' means 'I'm here'. Raising your hand slightly while saying it is more natural than shouting.

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the restroom near here?
Excuse me, your wallet fell.
Excuse me, may I sit here?
Excuse me! The bus is about to leave.
Excuse me, please take a photo for me.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 누가 저기요 하고 불러서 돌아봤어요.
examples.en: Someone called “excuse me” from behind, so I turned around.

explain: 이름을 모르는 사람의 관심을 끌 때 쓰는 말이에요. 식당 직원을 부를 때는 '여기요'도 많이 써요. 이름을 아는 사람에게는 이름이나 호칭을 부르는 게 자연스러워요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이나 가게에서 직원을 부를 때 특히 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Especially common for calling staff in restaurants and shops.

phrases.nuance_ko: 말을 시작하기 전에 조심스럽게 꺼내는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft opener before you start speaking.

phrases.en: Wait a moment, you dropped this.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가는 사람을 멈추게 하며 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to stop someone who is walking away.

explain_en: This is how you get the attention of someone whose name you don't know. When calling restaurant staff, '여기요' is also very common. For someone whose name you know, calling their name or title is more natural.

examples.en: Excuse me, is someone sitting in this seat?
Excuse me, may I ask for directions?
Excuse me, what time is it now?
Excuse me, may I pass through for a moment?

examples.ko: 죄송한데요, 전화를 잘못 거신 것 같아요.
examples.en: Excuse me, I think you dialed the wrong number.
Excuse me, I got in line first.

explain: 정말 사과하는 것보다 부탁이나 질문, 거절을 부드럽게 꺼내는 말이에요. 뒤에 하고 싶은 말이 이어지는 '-ㄴ데요' 형태라서 보통 문장이 이어져요. 처음 보는 사람을 부를 때는 '저기요, 죄송한데요'처럼 같이 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: Excuse me, what time is it?
phrases.nuance_ko: 모르는 사람에게 말을 걸 때 쓰는 공손한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite opener when speaking to a stranger.

phrases.en: Sorry, but please help me for a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '죄송한데요'보다 조금 더 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bit more formal than '죄송한데요' when making a request.

phrases.en: Sorry, but can you help me with this?
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for asking a friend a favor.

explain_en: Rather than a real apology, it is a cushion that softens a request, question or refusal. Because it has the '-ㄴ데요' ending, the sentence normally continues with what you want to say. When calling a stranger you can combine it, as in '저기요, 죄송한데요'.

examples.en: Excuse me, could you give me just a glass of water?
Could you give me the receipt too?

examples.ko: 죄송한데 사진 한 장만 찍어 주시겠어요?
examples.en: Sorry, could you take one photo for me?
Could you show me the menu again?
Could you speak a little more slowly?
Could you change the seats a bit for me?

explain: '주세요'보다 한 단계 더 공손하게 부탁하는 말이에요. 물건을 달라고 할 때는 '물을 주시겠어요?', 행동을 부탁할 때는 '-아/어 주시겠어요?'로 써요. 직원이나 처음 보는 사람, 어른에게 부탁할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Excuse me, please give me this book.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주시겠어요'보다 덜 공손하지만 가게나 식당에서 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less polite than '주시겠어요', but the most common form in shops and restaurants.
Like '주시겠어요', a polite way to ask if someone can do it.

phrases.example: 친구에게 물어요. 물 좀 줄 수 있어요?
phrases.en: I ask a friend: Can you give me some water?
phrases.nuance_ko: 높이지 않는 말이라 또래나 아랫사람에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It doesn't use honorifics, so use it with peers or younger people.

explain_en: It is a request one step more polite than '주세요'. For asking for an object, say '물을 주시겠어요?', and for asking someone to do something, use '-아/어 주시겠어요?'. It suits staff, strangers and elders.

examples.en: I study hard every day.
My husband works hard at the office.
I have an exam, so I'm studying hard these days.

examples.ko: 이번에는 열심히 해서 꼭 잘할 거예요.
examples.en: This time I'll work hard and do well for sure.
The kids are running around hard on the playground.

explain: “열심히”는 노력이고 “잘”은 실력이에요. 열심히 해도 잘 못 할 수 있어요. 그래도 열심히 하는 건 좋은 거예요.

dict_examples.ko: 그는 기관수가 되기 위해서 소학교만 나와 가지고 열심히 공부했었다.
dict_examples.en: He had only finished elementary school but studied hard to become an engineer.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 열심히 is about effort and 잘 is about skill. You can work hard and still not be good yet, but effort is still praised.

examples.en: This watermelon is really sweet.
Summer Korean melons are very sweet.

explain: ‘달아요’는 설탕 같은 단맛이에요. 기본형이 ‘달다’라서 꾸밀 때는 ㄹ이 빠져 ‘단 음식’이 돼요. 맛있게 달면 ‘달콤해요’, 너무 달면 ‘너무 달아요’라고 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 케이크가 달아요? — 아니요, 별로 안 달아요.
dict_examples.en: Is the cake sweet? — No, not very.
Roasted sweet potatoes are really sweet.

explain_en: 달아요 means sweet like sugar. The base form is 달다, so the ㄹ drops before a noun: 단 음식 (sweet food). Pleasantly sweet is 달콤해요; overly sweet is 너무 달아요.

examples.ko: 포장 직원의 한마디에서 뜻밖의 묘안이 나왔다.
examples.en: An unexpected clever idea came out of a single remark from a packing worker.

examples.ko: 아무리 생각해도 마땅한 묘안이 떠오르지 않아요.
examples.en: However much I think, no suitable clever idea comes to mind.

examples.ko: 마감이 내일인데 묘안이 있으면 같이 이야기해 보죠.
examples.en: The deadline is tomorrow, so if you have a clever idea, let's talk about it together.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 빈 시간에 할인해 주는 묘안으로 손님을 늘렸습니다.
examples.en: That shop increased its customers with a clever idea of offering discounts in quiet hours.

examples.ko: 묘안이라고 내놓은 방법이 알고 보니 비용이 더 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: The method presented as a clever idea turned out to cost even more.

explain: 묘(妙)는 '신기하고 뛰어나다'는 뜻이에요. 묘안은 깜짝 놀랄 만큼 좋은 생각이라서 평범한 아이디어에는 잘 안 써요. '묘안이 떠오르다/나오다', '묘안을 짜내다'처럼 말해요.

dict_examples.en: To come up with a clever idea.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: To rack one's brains for a clever idea.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 이렇다 할 신통한 묘안이 떠오르지 않았다.
dict_examples.en: No particularly brilliant idea came to mind.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 묘(妙) means 'wonderfully clever'. 묘안 is an idea good enough to surprise people, so it is not used for ordinary ideas. Typical: 묘안이 떠오르다/나오다, 묘안을 짜내다.
